PerioChip is used by inserting 1 to 8 chips into periodontal pockets with a depth greater than 5 mm, and this procedure can be repeated every 3 months. 3. Chlorhexidine oral rinse is used to alleviate oral mucositis associated with cytoreductive therapy in patients undergoing conditioning for bone marrow transplantation. However, its safety and efficacy in this context have not been established. 4. Chlorhexidine oral rinse reduces the effects of allogeneic cultured keratinocytes/fibroblasts in bovine collagen. This is contraindicated. If exposure occurs, the wound should be thoroughly irrigated with saline, and an appropriate wash-out period should be allowed before applying Gintuit. 5. Chlorhexidine oral rinse decreases the efficacy of the BCG live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This is contraindicated, and live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 6. Chlorhexidine oral rinse reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This is contraindicated, and live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 7. Chlorhexidine oral rinse decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Chlorhexidine oral rinse decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Chlorhexidine oral rinse increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Chlorhexidine oral rinse decreases the levels or effects of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 11. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Chlorhexidine oral rinse decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Chlorhexidine oral rinse decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 15. Chlorhexidine oral rinse decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 20. Chlorhexidine oral rinse decreases the levels or effects of vitamin K1 (phytonadione) by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 21. Chlorhexidine oral rinse may cause increased tartar accumulation on teeth, oral and skin irritation, tooth staining, bronchitis, altered taste perception, toothache, increased calculus formation, stomatitis, gingivitis, glossitis, aphthous ulcers, dry mouth, hypesthesia, glossal edema, paresthesia, desquamation, coated tongue, keratinization, geographic tongue, and mucocele. 22. Serious allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. Symptoms may include wheezing, difficulty breathing, facial edema, hives, severe rash, hypotension, and shock. 23. Staining of oral surfaces, such as teeth, mucosa, and the dorsum of the tongue, may occur as early as one week after therapy begins. This is more pronounced with heavy plaque accumulation or rough dental fillings. While the stain does not have a clinically adverse effect, it may be permanent, particularly in patients with frontal restorations. 24. Chlorhexidine is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Its excretion in breast milk is unknown, so it should be used with caution during lactation. 25. Chlorhexidine is a polybiguanide antiseptic and antimicrobial agent with bactericidal activity. It binds to negatively charged bacterial cell walls and extracellular microbial complexes. 26. Approximately 30% of chlorhexidine is retained in the oral cavity after rinsing and is slowly released into oral fluids. It is poorly absorbed systemically. 27. Detectable plasma levels of chlorhexidine are not present 12 hours after oral rinsing. 28. Chlorhexidine is primarily excreted in feces (~90%) and minimally in urine (<1%). 29.
